LongDescription: The ship's system detects a concentration of uncatalogued bio-signatures at this location. Sending a research team is advised.

While following the animals they were researching, the team discovered an entrance to an abandoned alien facility. There are some inscriptions on the door that they think they can decipher if given enough time; however, the animals are moving away.
The alien facility might contain useful data or resources. The team is authorized to break the door.
When the smoke clears, the team discovers a large number of containers that were shattered by the blast. Most of them were empty — except for one, which housed a curious artifact.
The inscriptions can offer insight into the culture and thought processes of E.T.s that the Behemoth might meet.

After employing some lateral thinking, the team finally makes sense of the inscription. It's marking the location as a depleted stash and has the coordinates of another, stocked one. The team soon finds the other stash and recovers useful materials.
Learning more about the biosphere should remain the crew's priority. The facility's owners won't be happy if they find it raided.
After following the animals for some time, the team saw an opportunity to hunt one of them to bring back to the Zephyrus for further research — and, possibly, as a meal.
We're detecting an extensive cave system at these coordinates. Our sensors are inadequate for scanning it at this distance. The entrance is marked for potential exploration.
The crew has entered the cave system and is reporting a hive-like structure that doesn't match anything in our records. It appears dormant — for now.
There's no need to disturb the hive. It's better to focus on gathering useful minerals.
Working carefully, the crew has managed to extract a decent amount of processable ores. The hive remained dormant for the duration.
We can't pass up an opportunity to study a new life-form. Samples of the hive and its inhabitants will be appreciated.

After dissecting the fleshy outer layers of the hive, the crew has found millions of insectoid organisms that seem to be hibernating. They're delivering samples of the hive and its inhabitants to the Behemoth as we speak.
Whatever it is, exploring the cave while it's around is too risky. Bring it down.

Several carefully-placed low-yield charges have effectively vaporized the hive along with its inhabitants. At the core of the hive, the team found an artifact that the creatures were clustered around. The artifact will be shortly delivered to the Behemoth.
We've detected abnormalities in the island's surface. They're too regular to be natural, so we're expecting this to be an archaeological site. Sending a research team is advised.

The research team has discovered a building that they think was used as a beacon. It's inactive and weather-worn, but in relatively good shape — there are multiple devices that can be useful aboard the Behemoth. The team also thinks they can repair and reactivate the beacon, and are asking for advice.
The beacon should be fixed. Whoever built it intended for it to be useful.

The crew eventually manages to figure out why the beacon went out and how to fix it. The beacon starts emitting measured signals on exotic frequencies, though nothing else seems to change in the moment.
The beacon should be adapted into a relay for the Behemoth's scanning systems.

Once connected to the beacon's infrastructure, the AI core has repurposed and rearranged the beacon's frequencies to meet the Behemoth's standards. The Behemoth's effective control range has increased.
We need all the technology we can gather. Dismantle the beacon for parts.
The crew carefully dismantles the equipment left behind by the beacon's builders. Some of the recovered components appear to be compatible with the Behemoth's systems.
We're picking up a Zephyrus lifepod's distress beacon. Initiating rescue protocols. Medical personnel alerted. Recovery crew on standby.

The recovery crew reports that the lifepod is surrounded by large flat rocks, which are painted with biohazard signs and angry faces. The crew expects that there are survivors nearby, though nobody is answering any of their broadband calls.
Looking for survivors is the priority here. Scour the area.

The crew has found survivors, but they're in bad shape. Their bodies have undergone significant physical changes after apparently being infested by unknown parasites. To stop their bodies from any further transformation, your crew has put the rescued people into a cryocapsule. Now, it is up to the doctors to save these unlucky hosts of an unknown parasitic lifeform.
The lifepod may have some clues about what happened to the survivors. It must be investigated.

The lifepod is a mess. From what the crew can tell, the survivors used it as a home but have since abandoned it. The interior of the lifepod is covered in slime and dead larval-like organisms. The crew suspects that the survivors didn't make it and focuses on gathering samples of the biomass inside the lifepod.
Whoever marked the lifepod may not want to be found, but they still can use some help.

The crew has left a set of survival gear, medicine, and some other supplies near the lifepod. They report seeing a figure approach the cache as they were leaving, but they decided to let the survivor be.
This is the crash site of a large piece of the Zephyrus's superstructure. Something useful can be salvaged from the wreck. Sending a recovery crew is recommended.

The team confirms finding a generally intact section of the Zephyrus. They're also seeing the tracks of a large predator that has made its lair in the wreckage. Scavenging while it's present is going to be a risky endeavor.
The simplest solution is often the best. The creature must be dealt with.

The crew opened fire at the first sight of the creature, scaring it with pain and loud noises, and chasing it away from the wreck. Sadly, the encounter happened in the data room, and the hard drives were irreparably damaged by all that shooting.      The crew has scavenged whatever parts and materials survived the volley of bullets.
The crew can reactivate the Zephyrus's security system, which can help deal with the creature.

With a bit of rewiring and elbow grease, the crew was able to boot up the Zephyrus' defence systems. The creature stood no chance. The crew managed to access the records in the data room that served as its lair and extracted useful blueprints.
It's possible to avoid the creature entirely by using the crew's knowledge of the Zephyrus.
The crew managed to avoid being noticed by the creature and found a well-stocked storage room. They're transporting its contents back to the Zephyrus.
Our sensors are picking up something that looks like a crash site. There are no signs of sentient activity at the site. Sending a research team is advisable.
The team reports the debris of an ancient non-human vessel in the crater.
Performing a complete analysis of the vessel's structure may yield data that can aid in our own research and development.
The analysis is complete. The team has transmitted the data to the R&D Lab, and our scientists are already working on it.
There's a faint energy signature inside the vessel's structure. The team theorizes it can be a power source; they can attempt to extract it.

The team has broken through the vessel's hull into what seems to be an energy cell compartment. With a bit of work, they've adapted some of the still-working power cells to function within the Behemoth's systems. The power sources are ready for retrieval.
There are traces of exotic radiation in the area, likely produced by something aboard the vessel. The team could investigate the radiation's effects on the local materials and organisms.

The crew hasn't found any abnormalities in living organisms. However, there are fractal patterns in some minerals that can be tracked up to the molecular and even atomic level. Their observations have been uploaded into the Behemoth's databanks for further analysis.
The ship's systems detect anomalous readings on this island.
The island has a strong electromagnetic field that's responsible for the wide variety of local anomalies, such as pockets of gravity-related distortions and powerful spontaneous electric discharges.
Test the effect of the local anomalies on Basic Extractors. It might be useful to learn more about the integrity limitations of Extractors.
The Basic Extractor you sent straight into the anomaly has been charged with so much energy that it is now a Battery Block.
It should be useful to learn more about these anomalies and their effect on the electronic systems.

When in contact with the anomaly, the Electronic Components get overcharged with so much energy that they explode. During the test trials, the scouts managed to retrieve a few of these experimental bombs.
How would a Biochemical Compound react to a localized energy storm? Only one way to find out.
When in contact with the anomaly, the Biochemical Compounds get charged with so much energy that they can now be used as power sources.
The ship's systems detect a concentration of uncatalogued bio-signatures at this location. Sending a research team is advised.
The team reports a rich ecosystem at their location. They are excited to proceed with their research and collection of samples.
The crew has discovered several organisms that have been previously approved as a food source. They're thinking about preparing them in the field and delivering ready-to-eat meals to the Behemoth.
The crew encourages the delivery of the harvested food to be as quick and efficient as possible to preserve its, as they describe it, "succulent" taste.
The crew encourages the delivery of the harvested food to be as quick and efficient as possible to preserve its, as they describe it, "succulent" taste.
The crew has identified several mounds of refuse around mono-species colonies. They believe that studying it will give them a better understanding of the creatures' digestive system and diet.

The crew's report lacks the initial scientific enthusiasm. They request the showers to be available by the time they get back to the Zephyrus and claim that no matter the value of such research (even if it will save the universe, they say), they will never go back to studying the fecal samples of this particular species.

The crew's report lacks the initial scientific enthusiasm. They request the showers to be available by the time they get back to the Zephyrus and claim that no matter the value of such research (even if it will save the universe, they say), they will never go back to studying the fecal samples of this particular species.

An organism that the crew was planning to investigate has, apparently, made its burrow in an especially deep fissure. The crew insists that remotely observing this particular specimen is crucial to their mission.

The data the crewmembers are sending back is truly captivating: the organism has a unique approach to altering its environment to fit its needs. The R&D team already has some ideas on how to implement it into their next project.

The data the crewmembers are sending back is truly captivating: the organism has a unique approach to altering its environment to fit its needs. The R&D team already has some ideas on how to implement it into their next project.
The team thinks they're being followed by someone sentient. They don't think the pursuer is malicious and are thinking about contacting them.
The "pursuer" turned out to be a Knidaria researcher who's eager to join the Behemoth's crew. The crew is bringing them aboard.
The "pursuer" turned out to be a Knidaria researcher who's eager to join the Behemoth's crew. The crew is bringing them aboard.
The site is populated by a large number of non-motile scavenger organisms. The crew wants to collect samples of what appear to be their reproductive organs.
The crew has easily gathered enough "fruit" to fill several containers. The "harvest" is ready to be taken back to the Behemoth.
The crew has easily gathered enough "fruit" to fill several containers. The "harvest" is ready to be taken back to the Behemoth.

The team has found a large population of previously identified antiseptic-producing organisms. They can process them into usable medicine, but the procedure must be completed on-site: the organisms quickly lose their potency after being harvested.
The crew reports an acceptable yield of medical supplies from the site. They've marked the containers for pickup.
The crew reports an acceptable yield of medical supplies from the site. They've marked the containers for pickup.
A strange maze of caves zigzags through this island's body.

As the scouts delve deeper into the dark caves, whose cold walls are adorned with faded carvings and primitive paintings, they hear a continuous echo of voices from farther along the tunnel. At first, it sounds gibberish, but as the scouts draw nearer, spurred by curiosity, they start to catch familiar words from languages spoken by human nations. And then, indeed, they see a group of people... all wearing Zephyrus's uniform.     The strangers look worse for wear, dazed, lost, and confused, raving like lunatics. When they see your scouts, they close in, howling in madness.
The scouts should try to calm down the crazed strangers. Maybe a gift of food, as a gesture of peaceful intentions, should pacify them.

The sight of food works like a charm for these tormented strangers. They happily accept the gift and stop being a threat. When asked how they ended up here, they blink in confusion. They can't remember but the endless tunnels they followed for... hours? Days? Surely, not more than a few days? And what was before that? A ship, oh, yes, a ship on water and before that in space... or was it all a dream, too?      On the way back, they also show the tunnels criss-crossed with golden lines they've stumbled upon recently. There, the scouts discover a gold and iron deposit.
Send an armed support group and protect the scouts.

The hungry and tired men are no match for your people. They run away into the caves from you, possibly to never see the light of day ever again.      One of them hauled something on the back and dropped it while fleeing. A few bars of Eldritium clatter on the ground.
Order the scouts to retreat through a different tunnel, and then send someone capable to find them and lead them out of there.

Finding your people wasn't easy, and you lost hope a couple of times. But then, your search group manages to find your lost crew members.      In their retreat, the scouts stumble across a rich deposit of Iron, Sulfur, and Hydrocarbons.       As for those strangers, they have not been seen again.
On the island's shore lies a large skeleton of an underwater species that catches the attention of your crew.

The scientists are excited to study the anatomy of the true giant from the local waters. A whale-like creature died a long time ago, but has managed to preserve the integrity of its skeleton in spite of everything. While one group studies the skeleton, another wanders around the island and eventually discovers an old cave system. As they start descending into the caves, they claim to hear an echoing ululation. A strange song reverberates in the tunnels, leading your people deeper and deeper into the caves.       Their journey ends abruptly at a dead end. The tunnel has collapsed.
Well-placed explosives can clear the path deeper into the caves.

The path is clear, and the tunnel leads to large vault-like caverns, partially inundated. To the surprise of the scouts, there are many more similar skeletons covering the floor. A true necropolis. As if those creatures deliberately sought out these caverns to find the final rest.      In addition, there's a rich deposit of resources.
We can set up an extraction right on the spot to clear the path.

The path is clear, and the tunnel leads to large vault-like caverns, partially inundated. To the surprise of the scouts, there are many more similar skeletons covering the floor. A true necropolis. As if those creatures deliberately sought out these caverns to find the final rest.      In addition, the extractor accidentally taps into a rich deposit of resources.
This tunnel can be a part of a larger cave system. In that case, there may be another way in.

Roaming about, the scouts find another entrance into the caves. The tunnel leads to large vault-like caverns, partially inundated. To the surprise of the scouts, there are many more similar skeletons covering the floor. A true necropolis. As if those creatures deliberately sought out these caverns to find the final rest.      In addition, passing by that serpentine tunnel, the scouts find all kinds of mineral deposits.
We've detected abnormalities in the island's surface. They're too regular to be natural, so we're expecting this to be an archaeological site. Sending a research team is advised.

The team has begun their excavation and reports promising initial results. They have uncovered several structurally preserved vaults, whose architectural style and materials indicate the ruins to be of Primordial origin. Moreover, the automated defense systems placed therein are dormant.
There are several carved pillars with intriguing scribing on them. The team wants to attempt to decipher those glyphs.

The crew successfully translates fragments of the inscriptions, revealing them to be a complex construction plan written down in a poetic form. It seems that Primordials wrote and structured their working manuals as poems. This discovery provides insight into Primordial tech.
The team believes there is more to be found: a series of collapsed chambers beneath the ruins.
The chamber reveals relics preserved in sealed alcoves — artifacts of craftsmanship far beyond even the human culture. Some hold faint traces of unknown energy, sparking curiosity and further study.
Survey the ruins with scanning equipment instead of physical excavation. Excavating blindly seems like a poor choice.
The team detects energy signatures in the ruins. They manage to excavate several ancient power sources and can extract some materials from them.
Alternatively, the effort can be spent on salvaging the construction materials from the collapsed structures.

The materials are being prepared for transportation. The team warns that they've seen predator tracks in the vicinity and urges the retrieval crew to be careful. Luckily, nothing extraordinary happens, and the team safely retrieves the materials.
The team sees half-buried crates that appear alien to the ruins' architecture. They'd like to investigate them.
The crates are mangled containers from Zephyrus, arranged in what looks like ritualistic patterns. Whoever did that is not around, and the crew proceeds to salvage the contents of those crates.
A section of the ruins appears freshly breached by meteoric impact. The crew wants to investigate the fallen body from the sky.

To the team's surprise, the meteor that struck the building was a piece of the Zephyrus — more specifically, a section of the cargo hold carrying extractor capsules. The team has marked them for retrieval.
We're detecting an active Zephyrus's supply drop beacon. We can use all the materials we can get. Sending a recovery crew is advised.

The crew has a visual on the supply drop. Many of the containers split on impact and have scattered their contents across a large area. The team is conducting a sweep to assess what's recoverable, but they will need to focus on a particular type of supplies.
Open the pod immediately and inspect the contents.

The pod contains preserved rations, medical supplies, basic tools still in usable condition, and... survivors! A group of people from Zephyrus couldn't find a free lifepod and decided to leave the compromised ship in a supply beacon. Luckily, their plan has brought them straight to your hands.
Disable the beacon and analyze its transmission log.
The logs reveal the coordinates of other supply drops scattered across the region. One of them contains usable power cells, which are being prepared for pickup.
Scan the pod for hidden compartments.
The scanners detect a concealed chamber inside the pod, holding encrypted data crystals and high-grade alloys. Both science and engineering teams gain much from this finding.
We're picking up a Zephyrus escape pod's distress beacon; the signal is weak and distorted. Initiating rescue protocols. Medical personnel alerted. Recovery crew on standby.
The team has reached the coordinates and has a visual on the escape pod. Nothing indicates the presence of survivors. Further investigation is necessary.
Force the hatch open and search inside.
The crew pries the door loose and discovers sealed ration packs, medical injectors, and an intact survival kit. A modest but valuable recovery.
Examine the escape pod's emergency systems.
The power core, though damaged, still carries residual charge. Repurposing its components provides the engineers with useful materials.
Search for personal effects or logs of the crew.
A cracked datapad is recovered, containing fragments of journal entries and flight records. The information sheds light on the lifepod's origin.
Scavenge the hull for reusable plating.
Sections of alloy plating are pried free and stored for later use. They will reinforce the expedition's defenses and equipment.
Inspect the surrounding area for debris from the crash.
The search uncovers scattered toolkits, half-buried in the sand, and a still-intact water purifier. A fortunate addition to supplies.
Perform a respectful burial of any remains found inside.
The crew finds skeletal remains and conducts a solemn burial. Morale rises as the act honors the fallen and reinforces unity among the team.
This is the crash site of a large piece of the Zephyrus's superstructure. There could be useful salvage in the wreck. Sending a recovery crew is recommended.

Several modules have managed to survive through the ship's destruction and the crash landing. But now it is prey to fire. Putting out the fire will take time, during which many of the valuable items contained in those modules will be destroyed. Your crew can save only so much. What will it be?
Search the wreckage for intact supplies and cargo.
The team recovers crates of preserved rations, tools, and medical kits. These supplies will bolster the expedition significantly.
Inspect the damaged engines.
Despite their ruined state, the engines hold traces of advanced design — hybrid components unknown to the crew. The discovery may inspire breakthroughs in engineering.
Recover the ship's black box or data cores.
Against the odds, the crew extracts a partially functional data core. It contains fragments of logs, coordinates, and encrypted transmissions worth analyzing further.
Try to find survivors.

Among the wreckage, the crew finds skeletal remains and pieces of uniforms. Burying them properly seems like a decent thing to do. The crew pays their respects and leaves a prayer for those lost souls.
Strip the wreckage for reusable construction materials.
Large sections of plating, wiring, and structural supports are salvaged intact. These resources will prove valuable for future repairs and expansions.
Survey the wider crash site for external debris.
The search reveals scattered fragments — intact cargo pods and smaller wreckage pieces that survived the crash. These hold minor valuables that can be used on the Behemoth.
We're picking up chatter from a mercenary outpost. It's possible we could hire someone there.
The outpost is bustling with activity. The landing party has identified several promising candidates that they want to talk to.
Aetherid
The crew hired an Aetherid
Crabari
The crew hired a Crabari
Human
The crew found a survivor of the Zephyrus crash.

The crew hired a Knidaria
