The crew hired a Nasobi
Unknown species settlement detected. Appears to be a small village clustered around industrial structures and a dock district.

A group of furry bipedal creatures dressed in complex, embroidered garments greets the team. Sensors detect strong musk emissions — scents — that change in deliberate patterns as part of their communication system, alongside high-pitched vocalizations. Real-time translation is possible.      The creatures call themselves Nasobi and greet the team at this East-West Trading Company outpost. The head of the delegation calls himself Stealitte the Silky-Smooth, and is awe-struck by the sight of the Behemoth. He proposes a trade deal. It seems these Nasobi value economic relations.
Stealitte offers to buy human-made alloys. This colony specializes in producing steel, and he is keen to compare our worksmanship to his.
The coins in which Stealitte pays you are made of some unknown metal or alloy. Maybe we should give it to our R&D for the test.
To produce quality steel, the Nasobi mine a lot of rare metals. Stealitte is willing to trade them for precious metals — it would appear gold and silver hold value everywhere.
In Nasobi culture, gold and silver aren't as revered as in ours. Nasobi still use it for decorations and in chemistry
Canned food is a rare commodity in the Colonies. Steallite proposes to buy it from us to provide a good supply in case of shipping delays
Nasobi, in return, sends us raw metals, direct from their smelters.
Nasobi trader passes you the letter from the Steallite, sealed by the East-West TC seal.
Stealitte, on behalf of East-West TC, offers to continue the trade. He asks if we can sell something beyond the raw materials and expresses sincere interest in Human tech.
For now, it's safer to stay on the same level of trade relations. We need to learn more about the Nasobi culture and traditions.

We can still sell steel. To be sure the Stealitte doesn't try to steal it. Too many steel puns. Anyways…      The reaction of the Nasobi captain shows, they expected more. Well, guess they'd have to wait. All in its time.
Providing some compounds to increase production efficiency is a minor intrusion. A safe next step in the relations with the locals.

As far as we can tell, the provided chems left the Nasobi captain satisfied. We still have a lot to learn about Nasobi communications. It's not a problem to generate smells they use for communication, but it's not easy to pick the proper smell in the right situation.
Sometimes, to fuel commerce, you need… fuel. An efficient energy source for the current tech level of the Nasobi can boost both production and logistics.

It's a bit risky, for it can also boost a war-tech. But we can cut the supply in case the Company tries to fuel the warships or arms production. Be it as it may, but the Nasobi Captain sure looks happy.
Incoming transmission from Nasobi Trading Post, a plea for help

A small East-West TC trading post is under siege. A roaming sea monster decided to claim these waters as its territory. It's defending it fiercely, attacking every ship on sight. Nobody can come to or leave the island, the supplies are running low, and the distance is too big for wireless communications. But the Behemoth is too large even for the Leviathan to attack, so the Nasobi hope we can help them break the siege.
We need to help the people first. Any other decisions will cause the delay, meaning more sick and starving on the island. The Nasobi workers beg your crew to take them from this island.

Nasobi boss isn't pleased with you decision.      "Soft heart is often a bad advisor for the Merchant, Captain. The low-borns can take care of themselves. The goods can't. If we loose them, we wouldn't be able to pay the low-born for their work".

The Trading Post chief asks to evacuate goods and equipment first. The Company will send the armored ships to deal with the monster, but operations of such scale require preparation. The workers can hold, but the drops in sales will be devastating for the Company owners.
Company chief is happy with your decision. He offers you a part of the evacuated goods as an upfront payment.
A small Nasobi farming colony hails us on open comms. The speaker is exceedingly polite and extends an invitation for dinner.

The Nasobi Noble overseeing the colony, Lady Farino the Fire-Coated, pleasantly welcomes our team, offering treats and showing them around.       The conversation soon takes a darker turn. As the colony grew larger, it ran out of farming land. They still need to provide the contracted amounts to the Company, but this means there's less food for the colonists. Both a breach of contract and a famine are bad options. Is the Behemoth, by chance, looking to hire new crew members?
Eldritium coins seem to be accepted universally, and Lady Farino will happily take nuggets of it as payment.
The lion share of the pay goes to the Lady of the Colony, but the willing workers are now free and will have their own paycheck.
The colony needs medicine, so lady Farino will gladly accept it as payment.
Lady Farino accepts your offer gladly. The medicine is highly valued in the colonies, perhaps because of the long and complicated logistics, forcing the colonists to rely on their own pharmacy.
Do we need to pay the landlady for her permission to hire free people, especially in times of need? It's for them to decide.
We couldn't keep this a secret. We helped Lady Farino, but we've done it behind her back. She's pissed off, seeing our actions as personal offence.
A Nasobi settlement.      They may be able to accept the refugees — our scans indicate that they're surrounded by farmed land.
Farino the Fire-Coated, Lady of the Colony, gives our team a cold welcome. She claims that hers is a small farming colony, and it can't feed any more mouths.
We can offer food supplies to last the refugees until the Company can pick them up.

A small vessel cathes up to the Behemoth, with a message from the East-West Trading Company. They're thankful for us rescuing their workers and providing them with necessary supplies. The vessel bears a token of their gratitude, and uniformed Nasobi quickly bring it onboard the Behemoth.
Threaten that if she won't accept the refugees, you'll inform the Company's Head Office about her actions.

Needles to say, lady Farino was furious, but has no choice but accept. Still, you aren't sure it 's the best course of action either for the settlement or for the refugees. If the Company wouldn't increase the supplies in time, all the nasty thing can happen on this remoute island.
We will not endanger this colony further. Another destination should be possible.
The refugees are a strain on the Behemoth's supplies, but it's the right thing to do.
A Nasobi outpost hails us.      Their coordinates match those of the destination of the goods we picked up previously.

Your crew meets the Nasobi noble in charge of the trading post. He thanks the Behemoth for the aid and expresses hope that the Company's armored ships will deal with the leviathan soon. His words don't sound sincere.
Our part of the bargain was upheld. Whatever happens next is between the Company and their people.
The Nasobi offical thanks us again and has a reward delivered to the Behemoth. There's no evidence of any ships being prepared to sail.
The Nasobi left behind on the island must be rescued. We will hold the shipment until battleships are sent to the area.

The official eyes the team with something approaching respect. After a short conversation with his aides, our radars detect a Company warship on course to the blockaded island. We can send the goods to the Nasobi port.
Finally, a new settlement ahead. Let's hope this is the final destination point for our Nasobi friends.

A Tidal Moon Trading Company runs this place. They are eager to accept a new workforce, and even willing to pay for them. However, the East-West Company managers among the refugees warn you not to do this. Giving up such a workforce will result in significant losses for the East-West TC. That, in consequence, will damage the relations between the Company and the Behemoth.
This long journey is finaly over. These people have found a new home.
Tidal Moon praises your wise decision and offers you a generous gratitude. The East-West nobles, however, aren't that pleased.
The East-West refugees can become part of the Behemoth's crew in full, if they so desire. They will, of course, be free to leave whenever they wish.

The Tidal Moon officials' mood sours, as does their smell. The refugees, however, look relieved. They will stay aboard and contribute as part of our crew. The East-West Trading Company may yet find a way to use them.
Nasobi trading post detected. They're hailing us, apparently already aware of the Behemoth.
Farino offers to buy the trinket. The offered price is surprisingly generous, almost like she's hiding real value of it.

Accept the offer. Fraud or not, for us it's a matter of the relations not the real price. After all it is just a small piece of the decorations and jewelry, received as payment. There are many like it... hopefully.
The deal is struck and the team makes it clear that they would not dream of stealing artifacts from their rightful owners. Hopefully, this message will be understood and spread around.
Politely decline the offer. Maybe it's more then just a decoration. We'd better check it out.

The result amazes the scientists. The thing wasn't made by Nasobi. In fact, the only known civilization able to create such a device is the Primordials. One can only wonder how it ended up within in the Nasobi trinket.
A small trading post with a merchant ship we met recently, anchored in the docks. Something bad happened here. Realy bad.

It becomes evident as soon as the team steps out of the recon craft. Some of the chemicals we sold to the East-West TC were transported here and were stored in a warehouse with none of the required precautions.       It's hard to to tell what exactly happened — an open fire in the room, an unfortunate chemical reaction or something else, but flame engulfed the warehouse and damaged the containers. Water only fuels the chemical fire, and the Nasobi are at a loss. Toxic smoke covers both the port and the town.
Aiding the civilians is a priority. We can treat any poisonings and burns better than the locals. We will establish a makeshift camp for the sick and wounded on the far side of the island.

A few moments after the team was done with the evacuation, the smoking warehouse suddenly burst into blue-green flames. Even a short delay could have caused new victims, but our timely action saw most of the population safe. However, the settlement is now polluted beyond any hope of recovery. Everything from the smallest trinkets to the largest structures must be disposed of.
Decontaminating the city is a priority. Only we know how to deal with the chemicals; let the Nasobi tend to their wounded.

As the decontamination team was at work, a new explosion rocked the town. As far as anyone can tell, the remaining pressurized containers ruptured under the heat. The decontamination crew, protected by the force fields, wasn't harmed, but a lot of Nasobi were exposed to the the toxic fallout from the explosion.
The chemicals were not evacuated from the warehouse and may yet pose a danger. Our crews can check whether that's the case.

The emergency team managed to drag out most of the remaining chemicals and extinguish several flame sources. While they couldn't prevent the next explosion, there were only a few containers left and the damage was limited to the building; the decontamination teams were done with the pollutants within the hour.
Girano, a Nasobi Noble who came with the hired workers, is causing trouble.
ShortDescription: A Gift from the Heart II

LongDescription: Girano the Salty-Black thinks he is the ultimate authority among the Nasobi crew members. He interferes with their tasks, gives his own orders, and punishes Nasobi workers at will. Not only does this disrupt the workflow, but it also affects the human crew witnessing it. Action must be taken.
This cannot continue. Girano will be relieved of his duties, constrained to his quarters and let off board in the next Nasobi port.
The low-born Nasobi crew members welcome the news of Girano no longer being in charge. The Behemoth's officers definitely hold more authority in their eyes after this.
Girano's superiors will know how to rein him in. We should contact the Tidal Moon Trading Company.

The executives in the Tidal Moon office provide sincere and very formal apologies for Girano's behavior. They call him off and provide small compensation for the troubles he caused. The low-born Nasobi appear relieved.
Girano should taste his own medicine. He will be punished for breach of subordination. This should make him think before acting next time.
Girano leaves the ship as soon as you enter the next Nasobi port. He is furious and swears to report everything to the Company. This will definitely change how we are viewed by the Nasobi officials.
The Nasobi refuse to follow orders and ignore their responsibilities. If left unaddressed, this may cause us problems.
ShortDescription: A Gift from the Heart II

LongDescription: The Nasobi openly ignore direct orders and leave their posts — not on some rare occasions, but in a systemic manner. However, they do not show aggression or act hostile towards the human crew, including the commanding officers who try to censure them.
We should clarify the rules. A set of guidelines, incuding punishments and restrictions, must be designed and communicated to the Nasobi to prevent them from breaking the rules in the future.

The guidelines training sessions showed a good level of understanding and a positive feedback from the majority of the Nasobi crew. However, overall effectiveness was mediocre at best — the punishments that were applied did little for behavior correction.
The problem may run deeper than is immediately apparent. We should study the interactions between humans and Nasobi to find the reason for the unsubordination.

A joint human-Nasobi study demonstrated that the Nasobi have trouble comprehending human communications in full, both written and verbal, since it lacks the scent component and thus limits the transmitted information. Non-verbal human communications, like gestures and facial expressions, are alien to Nasobi and take time to learn. The same is true about humans, who have trouble deciphering and, in some cases, even feeling Nasobi scents. While we can't recreate Nasobi non-verbal communication in full, we can now at least avoid misunderstandings and formulate communication guidelines.

We have enough on our hands already. The Nasobi should be able to handle isolated jobs with low responsibility and minimal outer interactions. Since they're farmers, they can be trusted with growing food.

Surprisingly, this worked well enough. Freed from the need to engage with complicated, borderline incomprehensible industrial procedures, Nasobi became more proactive and involved with their tasks. This is a good start and will allow the officers to gradually teach them to handle more complex procedures.
Nasobi Trading Post ahead. Not just warehouses, but also a steel mill. A large enterprise they have here.
Incoming transmittion: Welcome, Captain! The name is Stealitte the Silky-Smooth. I've heard of your ship and the miraculous tech you have on it. Care to trade it for something of our goods?
Behemoth can provide you with fuel for your furnaces, and you, in return, can supply us with metal.
Great, Captain! We'll gladly trade.
Behemoth can supply thermoplastics, a great material for heat insulation, assuring the health and safety of the workers.

I think you misunderstand us, Captain. We are smelting iron, not babysitting some furry good-for-nothings. If some of them fall out, there are always ten new, willing to take their place. Still, we accept.
New Nasobi construction site.
Greetings, Captain! It's about time you arrived. We are building a new plant, extracting and smelting rare metals. We'd appreciate your help. Do you have other marvelous tech for sale?
Effective explosives to speed up the mining. Be careful, though. It is powerful.

This is amazing, Captain! Never seen so little powder making so much boom! And you were right. We should've been more careful. A few miners ended up under a landslide. But fret not. Those are replaceable.

We can provide recovery medicine for your workers. It restores energy and makes rest more recovering. This has no side effects and don't cause the addiction, however, you should control the distribution carefully.
This stuff sure helps, Captain. No complaints, no suspicious activities – commoners are greateful for your gift. The problem is, as they work more, we must pay them more. ho-ho!
We can send our specialists to increase the productivity of your plant.
Your guidance significantly increased the productivity, and gain praise both from nobles and commoners.
New Nasobi construction site.

After the meeting with the Factory chief, where he asked us for more Earth-tech, some worker pushed a small note into the hand of our ambassador. “Your thermoplastics saved many lives and eased our work. We are grateful that you care not only for the profit. Can you trade more of such tech? The work here on the new site is deadly hard, and we need all the help we can get.
Electronics and remote controls will make the production process quicker and safer.
Factory Chief Stealette doesn't seem happy, but pays for your stuff anyway.

We can provide recovery medicine for your workers. It restores energy and makes rest more recovering. This has no side effects and don't cause the addiction, however, you should control the distribution carefuly.
This stuff sure helps, Captain. No complaints, no suspicious activities – commoners are greateful for your gift. The problem is, as they work more, we must pay them more. ho-ho!
Nasobi city-state welcomes us. Steallite invites us to the meeting with the City Council..

We welcome you, Captain, as a good friend and a reliable partner. We'd like to offer you an even bigger deal. We need workers. The ones we have are lazy, incompetent, and rebellious. We know, most of the work on your ship is done by machines. We want these machines and are ready to pay for them.

We have tireless workers. They are capable of working in the toughest conditions. Still, they can grow tired, they can break and can be useless if cannot give the right commands. And yes, they are very expensive.

If Nasobi had any doubts about the purchase, the demonstration convinces them. The artifacts they offer you as a payment is more than equal value. Those are crafted by civilization far over any you've encountered on Keeling so far.

Back in our homeland, we had a saying: Work smart, not hard. You don't need stronger workers, you need better management. And this we can give you. But do not fool yoursekves. The machine can perform complex calculations but you still need a living brain to make most of it.

The new control system significantly boosted production level on the biggest Nasobi factories. The payment was fair enough, and we also got a small (or not so small) bonus. The installed system not just controlled the production but also send us data analysis on the Nasobi industry and production. "Learn not by words, but by deeds" - there's wisdom in these words.
The artificial workforce - is a complex technology, which require technological base and trained professionals to operate. It may easily be wasted or abused. Unfortunately we can't sell you that.
Ambassadors leave shortly after. No deal - no feel, as it is said. Nasobi nobles loose interest in further contacts, and you presume they are offended by you refusal.
Ambassadors leave shortly after. No deal - no feel, as it is said. Nasobi nobles loose interest in further contacts, and you presume they are offended by you refusal.
A Nasobi city-state. It's in disarray: lots of homeless on the streets, garbage, and rubble. Should we check it out?

Steallitte steps up to welcome the arrivals. Your Meds. It was too good for its own right. We limited the distribution, providing it only in prescript doses and everything worked perfect. Until someone decided, the stuff is too good to have in such small amounts. We guarded it well, so all heist attempts failed miserably. But we didn't expect someone will try to recreate it. And that someone did. With one small  nuance. Not one, actually. The fake drug was weaker, had strong side effecs and was addictive. It spreads like wildfire. Now it's everywhere. You must help us stop it.
To stop the mass spreading we need to study the drug and work on effective treatment. Cured Nasobi can form the addiction anew, but that's not our problem in the end.
ShortDescription: FORM Taskforce to cure the addiction

LongDescription: The treatment helped, but the collective trauma remains. The drug wasn't made by humans, but the nasobi still blamed us of what had happened. The crew members, who helped the sick, suspect it was the nobles' idea to create a replacement drug. They hired the chemists and financed the research. The problem was, the Nasobi pharmacy was on significantly lower level.      Maybe that's the reason the nobles were so eager to pay for our help but did nothing to refute the rumors, putting the blame on us.

We can research produce the medicine to make the Nasobi permanently resistant to the drug effects. This would be more efficient than curing each and every addict in the city. This will not restore the damage the drug had already done, however. And there's still an ethical question. Are we truly ready to modify another sentient beings?

Addiction left hundreds, if not thousands Nasobi traumatized, and the city-state in ruins. The good thing is, the immunity for the addiction is permanent, so the drug is permanently out of action. Those who spread it, wouldn't be able to do it again.

Addiction left hundreds, if not thousands Nasobi traumatized, and the city-state in ruins. The good thing is, the immunity for the addiction is permanent, so the drug is permanently out of action. Those who spread it, wouldn't be able to do it again.
Behemoth's engineers became very close with some factory workers. Nasobi are sharp-witted, clever and fast learning kind. They deserve better.

The engineers spend a lot of time explaining, how things were on Earth, about the rights, freedoms, and justice. One of the workers, Hadoku, are the most eager to learn and apply the rules the humans told him about. He seeks our support, but it may displease the factory boss, Stealitte. What should we do?
Help Hadoku with the organization of the Union and support their claims before the Factory management.

The uprising of the workers angered and frightened the nobles of the factory. They didn't dare to respond with violence but neither they accepted all the claims. The negotiations were long and hard and even the initial success are far from the decisive victory. One thing for certain: nobles will remember on who's side you are. As well as commoners.

Direct involvement in the internal affairs is too risky and may drag us into a conflict. We can be on the good side, still remaining neutral. We have our own problems to solve. Teach, instruct, consult - but not interfere.
Tensions are rising. The workers acted earlier than we expected and the confrontation became violent.
This is unacceptable. We can't be involved, this is too dangerous. We don't need enemies on Keeling, our situation is dire enough as it is.
A passing ship told us of the bloody rebellion on the mining facilty. Rebels were subdued, but some of them managed to capture a small ship and escape.

A Nasobi ship approached. No nobles there, just commoners, many of them exhausted and injured. Their leader is Hadoku, the worker who gave you the message. He ask permission to come aboard the Behemoth.

Hadoku carries a weapon, his hand is bandaged, apparently still healing from injury. Still he looks calm and certain:      We rebelled and captured this ship. We don't want to live and die under the will of the Company Bosses. We want to join you and serve on your ship.
We can take only a few. But we can supply you on your way to your new home.
Nasobi accept your help. A couple of them still want to join your crew.
We're sorry, but your actions are unlawful, and we cannot support you. We just can't make enemies with the Nasobi authorities.
Stealitte sends you a message:      It was wise not to protect those rebels. We've found and returned them. Those found guilty would be punished accordingly.

Hadoku looks at you with determination and accusation: You showed us the way. And then, you abandoned us. You can't just drop what you've started. His right. And no matter how we wanted to stay clear of the local politics, we're already involved.
This will protect you if Company tries to attack you in your new home. That's the best we can offer for now.

R&D has asked us to secure specific resources during our travels and deliver them directly to the lab. Each material is a missing key component that prevents R&D from making a breakthrough in one of the following research programs...
Iron is an essential base material used in many construction projects. We should extract and deliver a batch from the nearest suitable island when we get a chance.

R&D receives a requested amount of smelt-grade iron and immediately validates it fit for their work. After running a few tests, they find a way to improve some of the structures previously designed for construction. They provide new blueprints for the Construction team.
Our scientists and engineers can process this resource into a safe supplement. R&D requests a small series of prebiotic samples to refine the recipe they're working on.

The lab completes the final test and confirms the discovery of a new stable prebiotic mix suitable for consumption. It is highly nutritious and tastes much better than what the crew had to suffer before. R&D promises to provide a recipe to the cooks soon.
R&D also requests titanium, a highly durable material used in several construction projects.

Delivered titanium allows the R&D department to improve the damage resistance of structures. They share their discovery with the Construction crew, who plan to implement the newfound improvements in the near future.

R&D boasts significant progress in researching three new blueprints. However, they are able to finalize only one of the blueprints with the resources available. They ask you to decide which is the most beneficial line of research.
Build a production line dedicated to producing Extractor Capsules (the mining machines required for resource gathering on nearby islands and wrecks).

The first test run of the new Extractor Capsule production line delivers according to the R&D's best expectations. Now the ship will have a steadier supply of Extractor Capsules and therefore a more efficient mining program.
Install a food synthesis bay to produce rations, easing pressure on provision consumption and preventing any impending risk of starvation.

The synth bay produces a solid first batch, and Galley quickly integrates the new addition into their pipeline. As a result, there's a significant boost to the Crew morale, as the sailors are happy to find out that their food portions have increased in size.
Create a fuel-cell assembly bench to fabricate fuel cells for the Engine systems and power banks.

The assembly bench produces its first batch of fuel cells. R&D evaluates the performance metrics from the new stack and is satisfied with the result. Now, the vessel has a lower chance of being stuck in the middle of the ocean with no energy to continue the journey.

An R&D scientist has submitted a shortlist of deck construction projects he wants to personally supervise. He believes that observing the Worker Drone's entire construction cycle will improve the lab's blueprint-synthesis pipeline. We must choose which facility to prioritize.
Install a food-synthesis bay to produce rations and reduce pressure on stored provisions during long runs at sea.

The scientist records calibration steps, material handling quirks, and commissioning timings. He says it was 'educational.' Meanwhile, the crew is happy to have more food on their table. Two birds with one stone.
Deploy a Solar Panel to capture sunlight and feed steady power into the ship's Energy system.

Panels come online under clear sky, and the Engineers note an increase in stored energy on the ship. The scientist analyzes the drone's efficiency, then drafts a quick scheme of some vague improvement he promises to implement. Now you have to wait to see the fruit of that breakthrough.
Expand crew quarters and give the scientist a chance to study the Worker Drone close by.

The scientist follows the drone and records its every step, noting the things that can be improved. He is quite satisfied with today's work and promises a significant increase in the efficiency of Worker Drones. Meanwhile, the Crew is happy to have more personal space in the quarters.

The crew believes that the R&D department never sleeps, and you're eager to believe this myth yourself when you're approached by an R&D scientist who has three test runs planned in his head. But with only 24 hours in a day, he can only accomplish one research project. Which research should you prioritize?
Metal Construction Materials are an essential part of almost any building. Not surprisingly, one of the tests requires a decent amount of the material.

You provide the Metal Construction Material to the R&D lab, and they start busily experimenting with the new idea. They believe they can improve the flexibility of certain components thanks to a new alloy they've been testing. They share their findings with the Construction department.

One of the tests is aimed at testing the energy consumption and ways of reducing the currently inevitable loss of energy, spent by the ship's systems. For this test, the R&D wants to put the whole energy system under considerable strain. Do you approve? REQUIRED ENERGY: 300

The R&D puts the ship's energy system through quite a test. A few times, you thought that the scientists would burn the ship's internal wiring to hell and leave you stranded in the sea. But the worst doesn't happen. And for all your stress, you receive reassurances from the R&D that they've made a breakthrough in a new blueprint.
Nanostructured Sheets are an essential part of almost any building. Not surprisingly, one of the tests requires a decent amount of the material.

The R&D eagerly accepts a batch of Nanostructured Sheets and puts their theories to the test. They find a way to reinforce the structure of the nanopolymer and claim that this research allows them to create a new construction blueprint.

Mnemosyne reminds you of the importance of certain materials and how the lack of such materials might endanger the entire mission. The AI requests permission to create a crisis-proof plan of strategic item management and share it with the appropriate departments. But which department requires such a lecture the most?
Presentation line 1: Fuel Cells allow our Engine to operate and keep us on the move! PRODUCE: 2 FUEL CELLS.

Mnemosyne provides a detailed briefing with graphs, rates, and failure windows on the fuel cells' usage optimization. The AI also creates a strict set of rules on how to prevent unnecessary energy loss. As a result of this lecture, the ship receives a surplus of energy that can be used to introduce a new construction prototype.
Presentation line 2: Anything you need finds its way into Extractor Capsules! PRODUCE: 2 EXTRACTOR CAPSULES.

Mnemosyne designs a specific workshop teaching a more effective use of the Extractor Capsules. As a result, the efficiency of resource harvesting significantly improves, which allows the R&D department to design a new blueprint from the excess of materials.
Presentation line 3: Not the best way to fill an empty stomach, but hey! at least it's edible. PRODUCE: 5 NUTRIENT PASTE.

Mnemosyne provides a detailed briefing to explain how to prevent the risk of starvation. A two-fold plan is proposed. First, new food portions are introduced. Second, clever waste recycling is offered as a way to reuse the scraps left at the end of the day. As a result, the R&D plans to introduce an updated menu with various entries made of recycled food.
The ship's systems detect anomalous readings on this island.
The island has a strong electromagnetic field that's responsible for the wide variety of local anomalies, such as pockets of gravity-related distortions and powerful spontaneous electric discharges.
Set up an extensive monitoring system to study the island's electromagnetic activity.

At first, the unpredictable nature of anomalies and the distortions they caused in the scanning devices made it challenging to gain any useful data from the chaos of electromagnetic flashes. But eventually, the scientists managed to adapt to this shifting landscape of anomalies and improve the available data acquisition and scanning tools.
Observe the anomalies from a safe distance.

Your scientists establish a safe perimeter around the anomaly zone. By studying the behavior of local anomalies and their effects on the surrounding environment, they discover how to induce controlled versions of the anomalies' spontaneous energy spikes aboard the ship, enabling the production of a denser, higher-energy fuel.
Equip the scouts with Portable Force Shields and send them to survey the area and observe the anomalies.

During their field trip, the scouts were caught in one of the anomalies, which suddenly engulfed them in its electromagnetic storm. Their Portable Force Shields have stopped the onslaught of energy and saved the scouts, but not without a cost. The anomaly has somehow fused the Force Shields with their bodies, modifying their muscle and skeletal tissue with an additional layer of electromagnetic field.        The scouts are currently undergoing a medical evaluation.

A strange signal emanates from the island, leading deeper into the maze of caves. Dr. Mey confirms your suspicions that the signal is 'Primordial' in origin. You thought so, staring at the Prism and its colors reacting to some external stimulus.

When the scouts delve deeper into the caves, a loud sound rumbles somewhere below, causing the cave walls around them to buzz with vibration. Then, the ground beneath the team cracks and tears apart, and they fall into the darkness.      Luckily, everyone is alive. They see a number of tunnels leading in different directions — they can try to find a way out or try to climb back from where they've fallen.
You have two professional cave explorers among your crew who are confident in their skills to find a way out. They want to continue with the scouting mission.

As the scouts explore the tunnels, they stumble upon an artificially made alcove. The walls once bore some kind of engraved scripture, but what it was is now impossible to say, as someone has vandalized the structure. Nearby, the team finds Chemical Fuel and excavation tools hastily left behind.
Provide the scouts with Propulsion Kits to get out of the pit they're in.

When the scouts jetpack back to the surface, one of them shows a peculiar discovery from that crevice. An old and rusty MultiTool, human-issue. It must have been down there for decades, but how is it possible?      The answer escapes everyone.
Provide the scouts with Scanners to help them navigate the cave system.
As the scouts successfully find their way out of the labyrinthine caves, their scanners detect a rich mineral deposit.
A Nasobi outpost stands silently on an island. Two vessels are anchored by the shore. And yet, nothing moves. The streets are empty. Quiet, too quiet, eerily so.

The ships carry empty cages in their cargo holds. On the shore, the scouts find a trace of struggle in the streets. Several bodies of the slavemasters do a grim job of decorating the alleyways. And then, in the center of the outpost, the scouts find a large heap of rubble—some structure is buried beneath fallen rock from the cliff face looming overhead. As the scouts study the outpost, your ship's systems catch a distress signal from a human-issued lifeboat just for a brief moment before the signal disappears and doesn't repeat again.
From the layout of the outpost, it is clear that the local base of operation must be buried under all that stone.

The scouts unbury what little remains of the main body of the local slavemasters. Whatever personal effects or treasures had been stored inside were destroyed by the rock. However, a small human-made container and two extractors survived the damage.
In the warehouse, a considerable number of crates contain food supplies that are slowly spoiling, unused. We can load all these ingredients aboard and process them into something long-lasting.
The seized ingredients have been turned into Nutrient paste and Energy Bars.
That signal could be a fluke, but what if it is not?

As you keep scanning for any signal from the elusive lifeboat, a distress signal flares nearby and gets your attention. It disappears the next second and does not repeat. But that one second was enough for your systems to pick up the location.
A lonely Nasobi outpost stands on an island. As lonely towers a solitary ship over the shore. And not a sight of a single living being anywhere, not on the ship, not in the outpost.

The outpost is deserted. Many corpses lie and collect dust in the lifeless buildings. A log found by the scouts tells the following...      This was a pirate outpost, whose inhabitants died from a disease spread by "the aliens from the sky." Apparently, they found a sinking escape shuttle and looted it. The health issues began soon after, and believing that the items from the shuttle were cursed, the pirates buried them nearby. The location is marked on the map, which is incredibly difficult to read. And, in one of the buildings, heavy locked doors protect something precious to the pirates.
Blow away those heavy doors with explosives and find out what the pirates hid behind them.
The explosion damaged some of the containers stored in the warehouse, but you managed to retrieve the remaining crates with provisions and valuable resources.
Pick the lock on those heavy doors with the help of MultiTools.

The door was trapped. Once unlocked, it set the entire building on fire. Luckily, the scouts have managed to save some of the goods stored inside.      Why the pirates chose to leave these examples of human tech by their side and not bury them with the rest of the "cursed objects" remains a mystery.
Follow the map and find what the pirates hid there.
After wandering for some time in the vicinity and digging at least three different holes before finding the stash, the scouts retrieve the cursed treasure.
A cluster of squat buildings covers an island. However, you don't see any hustle and bustle so commonplace in a town of this size.

It is a deserted Nasobi mining settlement. Recently deserted, by the looks of it. Mining paraphernalia lies forsaken near the tunnel entrances, and the shabby buildings still shelter hastily forgotten trinkets in their nooks and crannies. In one such building, cages stand empty, gaping with their open doors at the scouts. Dirty plates and chains hint at the purpose of those cages. One of the scouts finds a dog tag belonging to a security officer from Zephyrus-01. To learn more, the team breaks into a slave-warden's office and finds a broken recording device.
You can break into the nearby storage that's been locked and try to find anything useful there.
In the storage, you find a few crates.
Armed with scanners, you might find something useful in the area.
Thoroughly examining the area, the scouts have found a number of valuable items.
Fix the microcontrollers and the recording device to learn the fate of humans on this island.

Once repaired, the recording device, in the ragged voice of an exhausted man, tells the story of the last days of an escape shuttle, of their lifeboat's unfortunate shipwreck due to a strange anomaly, and how the survivors were then miraculously found by a passing ship.       The recording stops there, not divulging the further fate of the shipwrecked people.
A local settlement stands seemingly deserted on one of the nearby islands. However, the ship's systems detect unusual thermal readings. Perhaps it is not as deserted as it tries to seem.

A small group of human survivors, whose escape shuttle had sunk in the nearby waters, managed to reach this island. They refuse to join your crew, fatalistic to the bone and believing the sea to be far too deadly. They want to continue to hide on the island, among the ruins. They offer a trade, asking for things that should help them survive.
Supply the survivors with MultiTools that can be used in a large variety of tasks.
The survivors barter a Fusion Cell in exchange for your MultiTools. They wave from the shore at your departing ship.
The risk of many health-related issues rises in the uncertain future of the survivors. MedKits should be of help.
The survivors are thankful for the MedKits and provide unused Cyberware that once belonged to one of their crew. They wave from the shore at your departing ship.
Portable Force Shields can protect from many external threats. The survivors are highly interested in obtaining them.
The survivors are thankful for your donation of Portable Force Shields. In exchange, they give an AI Core salvaged from their escape shuttle. They wave from the shore at your departing ship.
A distress call beacons your ship to this island.

In the forlorn ruins of a long-forgotten settlement, a small group of human scientists, stranded — their escape shuttle now part of the vast underwater expanse — has sent out a distress signal in case someone finds them. But they don't want to leave with you. What is the point when there is no way out of this planet? Instead, they want to spend the rest of their time here building a research station, in an attempt to find some of the answers they were looking for.
The scientists have been working hard on creating a functioning farm, but it is still not finished. They are happy to receive an extra supply of food.

The scientists thank you profusely for the food donation and invite you to dine with them. They tell you about the strange ruins they built their base on. The preliminary analysis indicated the settlement was seven centuries old. Not Primordial. At first sight, quite primitive in structure. And yet, the scientists show you the relics they found during their excavations, and these were evidently functioning and rather sophisticated electronic devices: scanners or portable holodecks.      Another group in search of answers that came to Keeling?       As the Behemoth starts to leave, the scientists wave you off from the shore, slowly growing smaller as the distance between the ship and the island increases, until they are tiny dots and then disappear completely.
The energy problem is among the most serious challenges. They are happy to receive a supply of energy resources.

As a token of gratitude for our energy assistance, they are providing us with some of their excess equipment. As the Behemoth starts to leave, the scientists wave you off from the shore, slowly growing smaller as the distance between the ship and the island increases, until they are tiny dots and then disappear completely.
The energy problem is among the most serious challenges. The scientists have tried to build a custom generator, but they lack the expertise in setting it up.

As a 'thank you' for our energy donation, we are rewarded with medical supplies. As the Behemoth starts to leave, the scientists wave you off from the shore, slowly growing smaller as the distance between the ship and the island increases, until they are tiny dots and then disappear completely.
The ship's systems pick up a distress signal coming from the island.

A lifeboat from Zephyrus-01's escape shuttle lies stranded on the shore. It is a shelter for a few survivors.      Apparently, an unknown disease spread on their escape shuttle, affecting the nervous system of the sick, paralyzing, and then killing those unfortunate to contract the malady. The people on the island didn't want to take their chances and hijacked a lifeboat, fleeing from the disease. They ask to join your crew, but your scouts report seeing strange fits of hand tremors among the unlucky islanders. When your team points that out, the people from the lifeboat, armed with Personal Defense Kits, suddenly attack and take your scouts as hostages.
Present the captors with "a cure" they want, laced with tranquilizers to put them asleep, and thus free the hostages.

As soon as the captors fall asleep, your scouts free themselves and report for further instructions. A quick discussion ensues about the fate of the attackers. While their aggressive actions warrant a punishment, their extreme circumstances must also be taken into consideration.      It is cruel to leave them here to die.      Therefore, it is decided to place the desperate survivors in cryocapsules to administer the necessary help once you have the means to do so.
Agree to provide the sick with a thorough medical examination and treatment.
The doctors manage to find the cure for this paralytic affliction and treat the sick, who join your crew.
By creating a distraction, you might give your scouts a chance to slip away unnoticed.

The plan works, facilitated by the deteriorating physical conditions of the captors. When a chain of explosions starts and distracts the armed strangers, the scouts jump to their feet and start running toward the recon craft.
The ship's systems pick up a distress signal coming from the island.

Once your scouts reach the island, they find the crew of an escape shuttle (nowhere in sight) there in a mild state of weird frenzy. It is like everyone has lost their minds, mumbling nonsense and gesticulating madly. It is also impossible to figure out who sent the distress call, as no one can communicate reasonably anymore.
Perhaps a quality time with other people, not plagued by the same insanity, will help these poor madmen to come to their senses.

The interaction with your crew helps some of the survivors to find their lost reason. They continue to be somewhat restless and anxious, but the worst seems to be behind them now. They don't remember how it came to this, and they are abhorred by the sight of their fellow crew members.      They decide to join your team. The others continue their descent into madness on the island, lost at sea.
This requires a medical intervention. Send these people to the Health Care Center.

Only a few recover after undergoing rehabilitation at the Health Care Center. They don't remember how it came to this, and they are abhorred by the sight of their fellow crew members.      They decide to join your team. The others continue their descent into madness on their island lost at sea.
Perhaps they need something to guide them back from their frenzy. A movie on a holodeck?

The magic of cinema works like a miracle on some of your unfortunate guests. Not everyone. Slowly, a few afflicted guests return to their senses, though not without a few lingering effects, such as general restlessness and anxiety. But the worst seems to be behind them.      They don't remember how it came to this. It's all like a bad fever dream. First, there was a despair, deep and blue like an ocean beneath, then there was the darkness of the senselessness.      They join your crew, while the others are left on the island lost at sea, to continue their descent into madness.
One of the supply beacons, standard issue, floats in the waters nearby.
The supply beacon appears to be damaged, probably due to a faulty landing. A stream of cache containers pours out of it. The situation calls for immediate reaction.
Fix the malfunction in the thrusters to activate them and put the supply beacon in a temporary hovering stand-by mode.
The supply beacon, propelled by its thrusters, hovers above the water. The new position prevents the remaining containers from spilling out of the beacon.
Patch the hole in the supply beacon and safely transport it to the ship.
The scout team patches the hole in the supply beacon, preventing any more containers from slipping away into the water. Once the supply beacon is delivered to the ship, its cargo is safely retrieved.
Order the scouts to crack open the sinking containers and save what they can.
The scout team manages to retrieve some of the goods from the sinking containers before they vanish below the water.

The likelihood of anyone surviving the spaceship's destruction is low but not zero: Zephyrus had self-propelled emergency escape pods and shuttles distributed throughout the ship for evacuation. Someone could have reached them just in time.      But what exactly could destroy Zephyrus, our most advanced and well-protected spaceship? Could the Behemoth be next? Learning more about what happened might increase the chances of survival for this ship and its crew. For that, the flight recorder and the bridge voice recorder must be retrieved.
Harsh conditions jam the long-distance signals. To pick up the emergency signal from the escape pods, a more powerful transmitter is required.
The transmitter has picked up several signals, all heavily distorted. For now, it is unclear whether any of them belong to an escape pod, but Mnemosyne will work on finding out.
Mnemosyne can analyze all the recorded data of the Zephyrus's destruction and predict the probable crash sites of its debris, including the pieces where the flight recorders should be contained.

Mnemosyne's processing power is not enough to calculate all the variables and accurately predict the landing sites of both recorders. It is further complicated by the fact that the fragments of Zephyrus are still in orbit and have yet to pass through the lower atmosphere and shatter.        For now, Mnemosyne has to prioritize a more important data carrier in her limited calculations. The flight data recorder is more promising as it should have technical details of the mothership's final minutes.        The landing site should be established within two hours.
An escape shuttle must be somewhere on this island, as this is where its distress signal is coming from.
Blood, claw marks, shredded EVAs, guts, torn limbs, and more blood greet your scouts inside the escape shuttle. Something has gotten to the space refugees before you.
Arm the scouts and send them to search the island for survivors (or their bodies).

Despite the lack of progress in locating people from Zephyrus, the scouts have had significant success in finding the predators, possibly responsible for attacking the escape shuttle. All they had to do was stay on the island long enough to become bait for the hungry beasts.      The ambush left two of the party severely wounded, but the team managed to fight off and retreat to the extraction point, leaving the island without discovering the fate of the survivors.
To access the shuttle's systems, cameras, and log, your crew needs to repair the damage done by the fight that took place inside it.

The escape shuttle's log accounts for six passengers, one of them a child.      The cameras show that two passengers of the shuttle had died before the creatures attacked. They bled from their eyes and were delirious. In the end, they grew aggressive and forced other passengers to flee.      The wild beasts only ravaged the corpses and did not attack any other member of the evacuation.      That's when the scouts notice the last clue. Each escape shuttle, specifically designed for Keeling in mind, is equipped with a lifeboat in case the landing happens to be 'watering.' And such a lifeboat is currently missing from the shuttle's inventory.
According to Mnemosyne's predictions, the section of the mothership containing the flight recorder should have landed on this island.

The scouts follow the column of smoke that echoes the trajectory of the fallen fragment. The closer they get, the more destruction they see. The blast from the impact has melted stone and banished the living elements from the location. Not a blade of grass has remained. Just pockmarks from stone-turned-shrapnel everywhere, leaving long-standing scars.      And then, a crater. A large, smoldering chunk of twisted metal lies inside. The dispatched scouts approach a burial ground of their mothership, watching it somberly — another reminder of what they have lost.
Six hours of painstaking and careful "surgery" are required to extract the flight recorder without any risk of damaging it.

Slowly and carefully, like handling a bomb that is one wrong move away from detonating, the team peels off layer after layer of metal, exposing a mess of fried spaceship's innards. In the process, they manage to salvage quite a few valuable parts and components that can be useful for our survival.      Finally, after long hours of exhausting dissection, the flight data recorder is retrieved.       It appears to be intact.
We have no time to waste on the surgical dissection. We need the answers, and we need them ASAP.

Tuuli, Chief Engineer, does her best to calculate the amount of explosive charges, as well as their placement, to keep the further destruction of Zephyrus's wreck under control. Despite her best efforts, all the fine elements of the spaceship that could have survived the fall are now beyond salvation.      The flight data recorder appears to have taken serious damage, too. Its integrity is compromised. It is unclear whether your team's explosive extraction techniques are to blame, but it is doubtful they have improved the situation.
Repelled by the overwhelming numbers of local predators, the scouts failed to discover the fate of the survivors. It is the time to learn from our mistakes and attempt again.
The island is swarming with dangerous predators. And somewhere, surrounded by violent beasts, a group of survivors might still be alive. Or so many of your crew want to believe.
The drones should not attract the unwanted attention of local predators and will therefore traverse the island more efficiently.
As expected, the drones are of no interest to the carnivores and pass through the island without a hitch. But after hours of circling around, they find no survivors on the island, nor their remains.
Protected by force shields, an armed group can easily dispatch the hunting packs of predators and provide the necessary aid to survivors if any are found.

The scouts move swiftly through the island, unhindered. Claws and fangs fail to pierce the force fields encompassing the bodies of the scouts, while the bullets find no such problem with the animal hides.  But all that bloodshed leads to nothing. Your scouts find no survivors on the island, nor their remains.
The lifeboat is feverishly tossed around by the legion of turbulent waves.

Your scouts reach the lifeboat and meet the survivors. But it is not the reunion they have been hoping for:      People on the lifeboat look horrible. Their eyes bulge in pain, rimmed by blood. Crimson tears run down and spread, like Martian deltas, on their puffed, inflamed faces.            The sickness has spread among the survivors despite their safety suits. It means your scouts are not safe either.
Bring the survivors to the ship and provide them with all the necessary medical help.

The scouts deliver shots of the omni-vaccine to the sick without much hope, as this cure only works against the known viruses. And yet, after the shots, the afflicted people seem to show general signs of improvement: less pain, less bleeding, and reduced fever.       As the scouts are about to return with the survivors, Mars Abbadie, the Head of R&D, advises you to isolate all of those people and prepare for the worst.
Keep your scouts away from the sick and use drones to study the disease.

Each survivor dies in horrible agony, screaming for help you would not provide. Their blood-streaked faces, their tormented cries — you don't think you will ever be able to forget. Especially, the death throes of that child. Not your, and yet, in that suit, so reminiscent of your daughter.
The fragment has sunk and now remains at the bottom of the ocean, together with the bridge voice recorder.
Somewhere below the waters infested with dead fish lies the bridge voice recorder entombed in fused shreds of the spacecraft.
Only anatomically-enhanced crew members can withstand the pressure and work under those conditions.

It takes a long time for the divers to cut through the multiple layers of metal. It is also quite a distressing job, as they report sightings of strange deep-sea fauna: ghostly shapes passing by in the distance.      When they finally retrieve the flight recorder, they are happy to leave. In the submarine, they detect something large on their radar. It is rising fast to the surface, in the direction of the ship.
Worker drones reinforced with force shields should manage to extract the BVR, no problem.

It takes a long time for the drones to cut through the multiple layers of metal. The submarine crew supervises the process, happy to stay inside their vessel and not be outside next to those strange luminescent shapes.      When the drones finally retrieve the flight recorder, the crew is elated to leave the depressing dark of the deep. Before they begin their way back, they detect something large on their radar.      It is rising fast to the surface, in the direction of the ship.
The fallen fragment of Zephyrus is the epicenter of mass destruction, surrounded by a field of dead, boiled fish bobbing on the disturbed water. It is also in the middle of the anomalous zone.

The scouts report malfunctions in their electronic equipment and strange sounds when using communication devices. Each crew member present in the recon craft claims to hear a melody, something from their past. It keeps ringing in their ears, at the back of their mind. Invasive. Persisting. Haunting.       The success of the extraction operation is at risk as long as the anomaly is active. But waiting might not be an option: the fragment is slowly sinking.
The scouts believe the sounds lead them on, somewhere. It must be delirium, but… this planet is quite strange. Maybe it warrants an investigation.

The scouts chase the ghostly melody, looping in their heads, taunting, calling. This madness continues for a while until the scouts triumphantly report having found the Source.        The melody... it is now heard on the ship, too. The song Liora loved to listen to. It is in your head, and her voice, bright and worry-free, is so real, you turn around to find her... but she is not there. Then the melody stops. The scouts report they have found a strange artifact. It appears to be the cause of it all.        In the meantime, a large part of the sinking fragment breaks off and sinks into the bottomless dark below. The bridge voice recorder was there, too. And it is gone.
The anomaly does not go anywhere, and meanwhile, the debris of Zephyrus is slowly sinking. We should extract the BVR while it is not too late.

Maddened by the ceaseless melody in their heads, equipped with tools that kept malfunctioning, the scouts have had quite a hard time extracting the target. And when they finally get their hands on the voice recorder, it appears damaged, too.      Not as badly as the previous recorder, though. Some of its data might be saved.
The lifeboat is tossed around by the legion of turbulent waves. Radio silence greets your ship.

Bodies of the survivors, who are survivors no more, cover the floor of the lifeboat's only cabin. Their eyes bulge in pain, rimmed by a dried moat of blood. Crimson tears have run down and spread, like Martian deltas, on their puffed, still inflamed faces. These people have fled from horrible death in space and on the island, only to succumb to a no less cruel disease.        Among those corpses also lies the frail body of a child.       It is not Liora.
Order scouts to take the samples for the R&D lab.
Having taken all the necessary precautions, the scouts extract the samples and deliver them to the R&D lab for further research.
The examination must be conducted remotely using drones.

Transmitted results indicate that the virus responsible for the death of survivors is a mutated (or modified) strain of the Ebola virus disease. It appears to be much deadlier and more contagious than its Earth-based relative.
The ship's systems pick up a distress signal from the island.

An escape shuttle with survivors landed on this island. They sent a distress call immediately, wishing to be found by the Behemoth. However, the island didn't treat the newcomers with much hospitality. The survivors came in contact with some poisonous representative of the local flora. When your scouts find them, they are in a terrible state. If not helped promptly, they will die.

The doctors run tests on the afflicted individuals and claim that the conventional treatments won't work. They want to try to recreate localized force shields on the cellular level, thus protecting their bodies from the poison.

The surgical operation is a success. All of the afflicted individuals survive, thus becoming a new addition to your crew. In addition, the experiment has changed their bodies, similarly to how Cyberware implants would.

The doctors run tests on the afflicted individuals and claim that neither MedGel nor MedKit can help these people. They offer a temporary solution: putting them to sleep until you have the means to cure them.
You give the order to put the found survivors into cryocapsules.
The doctors run tests on the afflicted individuals and find that the only currently available cure is replacement of the affected stem tissue.
The surgical operation is a total success. All of the afflicted individuals survive, thus becoming a new addition to your crew.
The ship's systems pick up a signal from a supply beacon that's landed in the vicinity.

Two supply beacons landed poorly. It wouldn't be a problem if not for the fact that one of them was transporting fuel cells whose integrity is now compromised. The fuel is leaking out, creating a dangerous scenario for spontaneous combustion and then an explosion.
Send specialists who can neutralize the threat of an explosion.
While preventing a potential explosion, the technicians fail to notice a pack of critters that, enticed by the smell coming from the compromised crates, has ravaged the food and medical supplies.
Open the nearest, most easily accessible crates and take what you can.
The scouts hastily grab what they can and retreat from the beacons. A moment later, the explosion shakes the island.
Remove the threat completely by sending the compromised beacon away with the help of the propulsion kits.

The fuel-loaded beacon takes off into the sky, where it explodes. A spectacular display of fireworks.       While your crew members take the moment to watch the spectacle above, a pack of curious critters, enticed by the smell coming from the compromised crates, ravages the food and medical supplies.      The other cargo remains intact and is successfully delivered to the ship.
The ship's systems have detected a supply beacon on this island.

The supply beacon's thrusters malfunctioned and failed to slow down during the landing. As a result, the supply beacon crashed at high speed into the island, sustaining massive damage to its frame and cargo on impact. Its momentum carried the cargo transporter into several more collisions before it ended up near the shore. A large quantity of its containers have been scattered throughout the island, carelessly dropped during that dive-bomb landing. The rest of the cargo — different tech samples — require repairs.
The containers that remain within the supply beacon contain a jumble of broken pieces of various devices. A few items can still be repaired.
Your people manage to repair several items and salvage valuable components.
Use Basic Scanners to find the lost cargo.
Equipped with Basic Scanners, the scouts retrieve some of the lost cargo.
Send the most experienced scouts to find the lost cargo.
Searching far and wide, the scouts successfully retrieve some of the lost cargo.
Deserted ruins rust forgotten on this island.

The scouts report that the ruins were once a mining Nasobi outpost. Its dilapidated warehouse still contains crates with materiel, mostly damaged beyond repair by now, but the scouts believe they can salvage a few things.
The scouts have found crude automated mining machinery. It can be refashioned into Extractors.
Your technicians manage to repurpose the found machinery into several custom extractors. They swear the Mass Driver will not be jammed.
The automated mining machinery ran on crude oil. We can extract and refine it for our purposes.
The automated mining machinery ran on crude oil. We can extract and refine it for our purposes.
The scouts have found many crates with spoiled food. However, it can still be recycled into Nutrient Paste.
All that spoiled food is delivered to the ship's galley, where it is processed into Nutrient Paste.
A wide variety of animals inhabit this island. A number of your scientists volunteer to lead a research expedition to study the local fauna.

A wide variety of lizard-type creatures claim this island as their home. The Jurassic island — your scouts jokingly name the place, as they report seeing some specimens that reach two meters in height and six meters in length. These large specimens, in particular, appear to be herbivorous, and many of them bear large scars, perhaps indicating the presence of predators on the island.     As the scouts look for the promising observation spots, they notice a series of trees adorned with animal skulls. It seems that these skulls demarcate a trail into the local woods. But where to?
Make a camouflaged blind from which your scouts could safely observe the local fauna.

The scouts spent hours in their blind, watching the large, lethargic anomodont-like lizards graze nearby. Every twenty minutes or so, these creatures would expel a heavy mist of bodily fluids from their pores into the air. And every hour, these creatures would leave the island and disappear in the water for thirty minutes before reemerging and continuing with their pasture.      For more details on the creatures, refer to the database entry on Geobranchiates.
Find out where the skull-garlanded trees lead to.

Upon closer inspection, the symbology carved on the skulls appears to coincide with Crabari's written tradition. And, indeed, as the scouts reach the end of the trail, they find a slipshod outpost with crude wickiups heavily embroidered with more bones. Next to it lies a wide, excavated area that seems to be a fighting arena — multiple dried ichor stains and mutilated carcasses, now preyed upon by vultures, cover the beaten ground.      In the camp, the scouts find a workshop full of broken weaponry, a bone gallery, and a larger lean-to where the Crabari must have slept. They also notice several trees bearing notches on their bark. The scouts spend some time in the camp, studying scrimshaw bones and the anatomy of carcasses, both local animals and a few Crabari corpses, before returning to the ship.
Find an area with high animal activity and place cameras and sensors there.

The cameras provide hours of wildlife documentary footage about the large, lethargic anomodont-like lizards milling about, grazing, and sleeping. Every twenty minutes or so, these creatures would expel a heavy mist of bodily fluids from their pores into the air. And every hour, these creatures would leave the island and disappear in the water for thirty minutes before reemerging and continuing with their pasture.      For more details on the creatures, refer to the database entry on Geobranchiates.
The flying cube is impossible to ignore. It awes and calls for your attention, beckoning with the unresolved mystery of its nature, like a giant cubic question mark.

The floating rock defies all logic. It does not seem to be a part of a local gravity distortion, as neither your ship nor the recon craft nor any other object except for the Cube is affected.      The entire structure is criss-crossed with holes, with the largest ones being two round horizontal shafts made of pure eldritium passing through the exact center of the Cube. These shafts are composed of rotating rings, most of which have holes of their own that disappear into the rock.      And it sings, the Cube sings! As the wind passes through each hole, a distinct melody is born. And all those holes, all those distinct melodies blend into a hauntingly beautiful symphony.
Have the dispatched team thoroughly examine the structure and document their observations.

Each ring of the shaft and each hole seems to contain Primordial script. As is the case with their writing, the text is always more than one thing. Here, it is a complex circuitry shaped like words, the sum of which tells a story.       The circuitry is dormant or out of power, its purpose unknown. As for the texts, each hole begins with different words. Tales, legends, myths, lectures, treaties on physics, history... never the same thing! But unfortunately, the scouts are unable to see the full thing, as the holes stretch into the rock and the words disappear in the darkness.
The Cube contains much Eldritium, a unique metal found only on Keeling. Your crew can extract it.
Mining Eldritium is not easy due to its hardness, but after a couple of exhausting hours, your team returns with a decent amount of the metal.
Use the scanning equipment to study the Cube scrupulously.

Each ring of the shaft and each hole seems to contain Primordial script. As is the case with their writing, the text is always more than one thing. Here, it is a complex circuitry shaped like words, the sum of which tells a story.      The circuitry is dormant or out of power, its purpose unknown. As for the texts, each hole begins with different words. Tales, legends, myths, lectures, treaties on physics, history... never the same thing! But even with scanners, it is impossible to entirely read any of it, as the holes stretch into the rock and the words disappear in the darkness.
